standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness of the base change along a surjective flat morphism, and descent of flatness for a finite presentation module
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Morphisms, label more-morphisms-lemma-flat-locus-base-change (proof line 6456); Limits, label limits-lemma-descend-module-flat-finite-presentation (proof line 6458)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first shows that flatness of the pulled back module along a surjective flat morphism is equivalent to flatness of the original, giving the sheaf property, and the second gives the limit preserving statement, following the same reduction as the dimension functor lemma.

core_obligations: Get the sheaf property from the equivalence of flatness for the pulled back module along a surjective flat morphism (proof lines 6452-6456).

Get the limit preserving property by reducing to the affine case and applying the descent statement for flatness of a finitely presented module, as in the proof of the dimension functor lemma (proof lines 6457-6461).
proof_roadmap: Sheaf property from base change flatness (proof lines 6452-6456).
Limit preserving by descent and affine reduction (proof lines 6457-6461).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the functor of points over which a module is flat is an fpqc sheaf, and is limit preserving under finite presentation hypotheses (statement lines 6441-6450, tag 05MD-adjacent). The proof reduces the sheaf property to the equivalence of flatness under a surjective flat base change and the limit preserving statement to the descent of flatness for a finitely presented module after an affine reduction. The two reductions are the substance, so the claim is H2.
